title: Ulyana and the Bakery
premise: Felix Villalobos has spent eleven years running his failing vineyard and his own heart with the same iron discipline, convinced that love is a debt he cannot afford. When a bakery lease dispute brings Ulyana Petrova—keeper of a letter he never received—into his orbit, he learns his mother wrote him a confession of the family's buried debts and a plea to forgive himself before she died. As the bakery's last lease deadline collides with the vineyard's creditors, Felix must choose between the legal victory that would save his land and the quiet justice of handing the letter's truth to the town. He signs the vineyard away, keeps the bakery open past the last train, and finally lets himself be known.
about_author: Coral Yarrow is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper editor who spent a decade covering lease disputes, estate sales, and the quiet dramas of rural post offices. She writes romances about people who mistake survival for living, and she still checks the mail twice a day.

chapters.title: The Letter That Waited
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Sorting eleven years of misdelivered mail in her dying bakery, Ulyana finds a sealed letter addressed to Felix Villalobos, postmarked the year his mother died. The bakery's lease expires in ninety days, and her landlord's lawyer turns out to be the same firm squeezing Felix's vineyard. The emotional beat: reluctant hope—two strangers bound by a piece of paper neither asked for.

chapters.title: A Muscle Like Any Other
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Ulyana arrives at the vineyard with the letter, and Felix's careful, trainable heart cracks open: his mother knew the debts were manufactured by a crooked uncle, and she begged him to fight, not hide. He refuses to read past the first page and sends her away. The emotional beat: denial sharpening into obsession as he rereads that first page nightly.

chapters.title: What the Vineyard Owes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Felix and Ulyana dig through probate records and old post office logs, uncovering that the uncle forged the debt—and that the landlord's lawyer helped bury it. The climax: at the lease hearing, Felix must choose between a settlement that saves the vineyard and exposing the fraud, which saves Ulyana's bakery but forfeits his inheritance. He stands and tells the truth. The emotional beat: justice chosen over survival.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, closing with Felix's letter back to her. The vineyard is sold; Felix takes work repairing the bakery's ovens while the town reckons with the uncle's crimes. On the night the new lease is signed, Felix finally reads his mother's whole letter aloud, then stays past the last train without apology. The emotional beat: release—two people who learned the price of survival choosing, at last, to live.
